clinician.final_diagnosis: Tension pneumothorax, possibly secondary to underlying COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old man with a 3-week prodrome of dry cough, fevers, and dyspnea (presumed COVID-19 based on clinical presentation and infectious diseases team assessment, though initial RT-PCR swab was negative due to delayed presentation) presented to the emergency department via ambulance with acute severe respiratory decompensation. He exhibited severe hypoxemia (SpO2 88-90% on 15 L/min oxygen via non-rebreather mask), severe tachypnea (RR 50 breaths/min), tachycardia (HR 150 beats/min), and clinical signs of left-sided pneumothorax (absent breath sounds, reduced vocal fremitus, asymmetrical chest expansion). Physical examination showed a central trachea and JVP 3 cm above sternal angle. Underlying imaging revealed severe COVID-19 pneumonia with widespread patchy consolidative changes in the right lung. On admission, emergency needle decompression was performed immediately using a 14-gauge cannula inserted in the second rib space at the mid-clavicular line, resulting in rapid clinical improvement. Within one hour, oxygen requirement decreased from 15 L/min to 4 L/min via nasal cannula, with normalization of respiratory and heart rate and clinical and radiological evidence of lung re-expansion. A 12-French Seldinger chest drain was subsequently inserted into the left axilla for definitive management.

final.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old man with a 3-week prodrome of dry cough, fevers, and dyspnea (presumed COVID-19 based on clinical presentation and infectious diseases team assessment, though initial RT-PCR swab was negative due to delayed presentation) presented to the emergency department via ambulance with acute severe respiratory decompensation. He exhibited severe hypoxemia (SpO2 88-90% on 15 L/min oxygen via non-rebreather mask), severe tachypnea (RR 50 breaths/min), tachycardia (HR 150 beats/min), and clinical signs of left-sided pneumothorax (absent breath sounds, reduced vocal fremitus, asymmetrical chest expansion). Physical examination showed a central trachea and JVP 3 cm above sternal angle. Underlying imaging revealed severe COVID-19 pneumonia with widespread patchy consolidative changes in the right lung. On admission, emergency needle decompression was performed immediately using a 14-gauge cannula inserted in the second rib space at the mid-clavicular line, resulting in rapid clinical improvement. Within one hour, oxygen requirement decreased from 15 L/min to 4 L/min via nasal cannula, with normalization of respiratory and heart rate and clinical and radiological evidence of lung re-expansion. A 12-French Seldinger chest drain was subsequently inserted into the left axilla for definitive management.
